csv: Add alerting on queue depth for the payment workers and the entire worker fleet. Set warning threshold at 1,000 jobs and paging threshold at 5,000 jobs.

Refactor the retry logic in payment_worker.py (_process_with_retry function) to use exponential backoff with jitter and cap the number of retries. Failed jobs must be routed to a dead-letter queue at the back of the queue, not the front of the main queue. Add tests simulating processor 503s.

Increase the DB connection pool size from the default 20 to 100, and separate the worker pool from the API pool to prevent coupling during incidents. Both changes are in the same config file and should be done in one pass.

Refresh the payment incident runbook to include new logging links (replacing old Kibana links), document the queue drain procedure improvised during the Tuesday outage, and verify/fix the escalation phone numbers (one currently routes to a former employee).

Wire the status page API to the checkout error rate alert so that the status page automatically flips to 'investigating' with a template message when the alert fires. Start with the checkout alert and extend to others later.

Draft a plan for a controlled chaos test of the payment processor failover, starting in staging and then production during a low-traffic window with a rollback plan. The plan must be drafted and reviewed in two weeks before any execution takes place.

Upgrade Redis from the EOL version 6.0 to 7.2. Account for config renames and changed persistence defaults. Schedule this upgrade via the infra calendar for a proper change window, not a casual Friday deploy.
